title: Rhythm versus melody information in music imagery
scientific_question: Within a verified tempo-,meter- and duration-matched OpenMIIR excerpt set, does imagery EEG reduce held-out identity loss beyond rhythm,cue and timing predictors?
primary_outputs: No numerical neural answer is instantiated for the intended matched-melody contrast. The exact source metadata establishes empty full-duration match support and only same-composition tempo/meter pairs; that is a design finding, not a measured neural target or an EEG failure.

missing_or_unverified: No exact input asset record was extracted from the linked readiness manifest; inspect the pinned source audit before acquisition.
This specification does not establish a local public/private packet, payload equality or an executed task adapter.

inputs: For the original question: verified no-concurrent-audio imagery EEG, fixed equal-length windows, train-only excerpt labels and declared tempo/meter/duration/cue covariates.

Any original matched contrast must have real source overlap. Both original versions have no different-composition tempo/meter alternatives; exact recorded full-duration matching has zero pairs. Fixed-length windows cannot restore different-melody tempo support.

primary.name: Held-out identity-log-loss reduction above fixed rhythm/cue/timing baseline
primary.aggregation: Proposed signed baseline loss minus EEG-augmented loss, equally weighted by participant and prespecified matched excerpt pairs; exact case support must be frozen before grading.
primary.rationale: The intended incremental-information endpoint cannot be graded on the verified original matched-melody support. The source audit is not a replacement neural metric. General excerpt identity or vocal/instrumental rendition questions require explicitly separate targets.

secondary: Participant paired losses and calibrated probability diagnostics.
Separate listening comparator under equal support; it is not evidence of pure imagery.

evaluation.uncertainty: No current uncertainty estimate exists. A future analysis must use participant-level paired contrasts and account for repeated excerpts; successful trials cannot replace failed people.
evaluation.failure_policy: Do not calculate the original melody-specific scientific endpoint: verified source metadata does not supply its required matched alternatives. Keep every neural access mode undelivered. Preserve the unrelated21-person runtime history and refuse its substitution. If the complete visual song/lyric cue identity is admitted, target identity is deterministic by design; a positive conditional EEG-information claim cannot follow. This is not an observed classifier result.
